sub_graphs.name: Gas Limit Configuration Update
sub_graphs.description: Defines the core specification for updating the default gas limit in execution layer clients from the current 36M to 60M, to be applied by the Fusaka hard fork release.

invariants.text: All execution layer clients must update their default gas limit configuration value to 60,000,000 (60M) gas.
The gas limit update must be coordinated with and tied to the Fusaka hard fork release.

pre_conditions.text: Current mainnet gas limit is 36,000,000 (36M) gas.
Execution layer clients have varying configuration formats for specifying default gas limits.

post_conditions.text: All EL client default configurations generate a gas limit value of 60,000,000 (60M) gas.
The new gas limit is active upon the Fusaka hard fork activation.

state_transitions.description: Default gas limit parameter transitions from 36M to 60M across all execution layer client configurations.
state_transitions.trigger: Fusaka hard fork release and client update deployment

state_variables.name: default_gas_limit
state_variables.description: The default gas limit value generated in EL client configurations.

sub_graphs.name: Backwards Compatibility Constraints
sub_graphs.description: Defines the backwards compatibility considerations for increasing the gas limit, including interaction with the proposed 30M transaction gas limit (EIP coordination).

invariants.text: A higher gas limit must not break any existing deployed contracts.
The scheduling of EIP-7935 must be coordinated with the proposed 30M transaction gas limit EIP to prevent new transactions from exceeding the transaction gas limit boundary.

pre_conditions.text: Existing contracts are deployed and operational under a 36M gas limit.

post_conditions.text: All previously deployed contracts continue to function correctly under the 60M gas limit.

sub_graphs.name: Security Testing and Validation Framework
sub_graphs.description: Defines the security testing methodology for validating the safety of the 60M gas limit increase, including devnet testing, adversarial block analysis, and incremental rollout strategy.

invariants.text: Devnets must be stood up with nodes running all combinations of EL and CL clients before the gas limit increase is approved.
Synthetic transactions must fill blocks to capacity during testing to validate network and node health under full load at 60M gas.
The worst-case block size at 60M gas must remain below the current 10 MiB CL gossip limit.

Adversarial block constructions that maximize worst-case size must not be a factor below 150M gas, as the current worst-case block size of 1.79 MiB would only reach the 10 MiB CL gossip limit near that threshold.

pre_conditions.text: Devnet infrastructure is available to run all EL/CL client combinations.
Synthetic transaction generation tooling is available to fill blocks to capacity.

post_conditions.text: All client combinations pass devnet testing with full blocks at 60M gas without critical bugs.
Any discovered bugs are patched by client teams before proceeding.
Gas limit is increased incrementally after successful testing.

state_transitions.description: Iterative testing cycle: deploy devnet, fill blocks, monitor health, patch bugs if found, repeat until stable.
state_transitions.trigger: Successful completion of all devnet testing rounds with no critical issues

state_variables.name: worst_case_block_size
state_variables.description: The current worst-case block size under adversarial construction conditions.
state_variables.target_value: Must remain below 10 MiB CL gossip limit

state_variables.name: cl_gossip_limit
state_variables.description: The consensus layer gossip message size limit that constrains maximum block size.

state_variables.name: adversarial_safety_threshold
state_variables.description: The gas limit at which adversarial worst-case block size would approach the CL gossip limit.

metadata.extraction_notes: EIP-7935 is an Informational EIP, not a Standards Track EIP. It does not contain code or formal function definitions. Subgraphs were extracted from the specification's prose describing configuration requirements, compatibility constraints, and security validation procedures.

sub_graphs.name: CLZ Opcode Definition
sub_graphs.description: Defines the new CLZ (Count Leading Zeros) opcode (0x1e) for the EVM. The opcode pops one 256-bit value from the stack and pushes the count of leading zero bits. For a zero input, the result is 256.

invariants.text: CLZ(x) must return a value in the range [0, 256] inclusive for any 256-bit input x.
CLZ(0) must always equal 256.
For any nonzero x, CLZ(x) must equal the index of the most significant set bit counted from the top (bit 255), i.e. CLZ(x) = 255 - floor(log2(x)).
CLZ is a pure (stateless) function: the result depends only on the input value and not on any EVM state.

pre_conditions.text: The EVM stack must contain at least one element before executing CLZ.

post_conditions.text: After execution, the stack depth is unchanged (one element popped, one pushed).
The pushed value is a 256-bit word representing the count of leading zero bits of the popped value.

functions.description: Pops one 256-bit value x from the stack. Pushes the number of leading zero bits in x. If x is zero, pushes 256.

sub_graphs.name: Stack Behavior
sub_graphs.description: Defines the stack input/output behavior of the CLZ opcode. CLZ pops exactly one value and pushes exactly one value, making it a unary stack operation with no net stack depth change.

invariants.text: CLZ consumes exactly 1 stack element and produces exactly 1 stack element.
Net stack depth change is zero: delta = 0 (pops 1, pushes 1).

pre_conditions.text: Stack must have depth >= 1 before CLZ execution; otherwise a stack underflow error occurs.

post_conditions.text: The top of stack contains the CLZ result; all other stack elements are unchanged.

fields.name: input
fields.description: The 256-bit value whose leading zeros are to be counted (popped from stack).

fields.name: output
fields.description: The count of leading zero bits, range [0, 256] (pushed to stack).

sub_graphs.name: Gas Cost Model
sub_graphs.description: Defines the gas cost of the CLZ opcode at 5 gas units, matching the MUL opcode. This pricing is raised from the baseline of 3 gas (used by ADD) to avoid under-pricing DoS risk, even though benchmarks show CLZ uses approximately the same compute cycles as ADD.

invariants.text: The gas cost of CLZ is a fixed constant of 5 gas units, independent of input value.
CLZ gas cost matches MUL gas cost (both 5 gas).

post_conditions.text: Exactly 5 gas is deducted from the available gas upon CLZ execution.

state_variables.name: GAS_CLZ
state_variables.description: Fixed gas cost for the CLZ opcode, set equal to MUL gas cost.

sub_graphs.name: Zero Input Special Case
sub_graphs.description: Defines the behavior of CLZ when the input is zero. The specification mandates CLZ(0) = 256, which is the smallest number after 255 and represents the total bit width of the EVM word. This design allows efficient byte scanning via '256 >> 3 = 32' and minimal bytecode for comparisons.

invariants.text: CLZ(0) = 256 (all 256 bits are zero, so the leading zero count equals the full word width).
For byte scanning of a zero word, CLZ(0) >> 3 must equal 32 (the number of bytes to skip).

sub_graphs.name: CLZ vs CTZ Design Rationale
sub_graphs.description: Documents the rationale for choosing CLZ over CTZ (Count Trailing Zeros). CLZ is strictly more powerful: CTZ can be derived from CLZ via the identity CTZ(x) = CLZ(x & -x) (isolate the least significant bit, then count leading zeros), but CLZ cannot be derived from CTZ.

invariants.text: CTZ(x) can be computed from CLZ as: CTZ(x) = 255 - CLZ(x & -x) for nonzero x, and CTZ(0) = 256.
CLZ cannot be implemented using CTZ alone.

sub_graphs.name: Test Vectors
sub_graphs.description: Defines the authoritative test cases for validating CLZ implementations. Each test case specifies a 256-bit input and the expected 256-bit output.

test_cases.description: Zero input: all 256 bits are zero, so CLZ returns 256.
Most significant bit set: no leading zeros.
All bits set (max uint256): no leading zeros.
Second-highest bit set: exactly 1 leading zero.
All bits set except MSB: exactly 1 leading zero.
Only the least significant bit set: 255 leading zeros.

sub_graphs.name: Security Properties
sub_graphs.description: Documents the security properties of the CLZ opcode. CLZ is stateless (pure function), has constant-time worst-case behavior, low memory usage, low compute cost, and low ZK proving cost, making it resistant to denial-of-service attacks.

invariants.text: CLZ is stateless: it does not read from or write to storage, memory, or any other EVM state.
CLZ has O(1) worst-case cost in compute cycles, memory usage, and ZK proving cost.
CLZ cannot be exploited for denial-of-service attacks due to its bounded, constant resource consumption.

sub_graphs.name: Backwards Compatibility
sub_graphs.description: Documents the backwards compatibility status. CLZ (opcode 0x1e) is a new opcode that was not present in any prior EVM version. There are no backwards compatibility issues since no existing contract uses opcode 0x1e.

invariants.text: Opcode 0x1e was previously undefined/invalid, so introducing CLZ does not change the behavior of any existing valid contract.

sub_graphs.name: Use Cases and Applications
sub_graphs.description: Documents the primary use cases that motivate the CLZ opcode. CLZ is a fundamental building block for efficient math operations, byte operations, compression, and data structures in the EVM.

use_cases.name: lnWad
use_cases.description: Natural logarithm in fixed-point WAD arithmetic. CLZ is used to efficiently determine the magnitude of the input.

use_cases.name: lambertW0Wad
use_cases.description: Lambert W function (principal branch) in fixed-point WAD arithmetic.

use_cases.name: sqrt
use_cases.description: Square root computation. CLZ provides an efficient initial estimate for Newton's method.

use_cases.name: cbrt
use_cases.description: Cube root computation. CLZ provides an efficient initial estimate.

use_cases.name: Byte string comparisons
use_cases.description: Efficiently comparing byte strings by counting leading zeros in XOR differences.

use_cases.name: Generalized calldata compression/decompression
use_cases.description: Encoding and decoding compressed calldata using leading zero information.

use_cases.name: Bitmaps
use_cases.description: Finding the next/previous set/unset bit in bitmap data structures.

use_cases.name: Post-quantum signature schemes
use_cases.description: Cryptographic operations for post-quantum signature verification.
